summary.text: Adam Helman is One Nation's candidate for Brunswick at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC reports that he served in the Royal Australian Air Force for over 15 years and now volunteers as a firefighter and as a school crossing supervisor. He was One Nation's candidate for the federal seat of Corio in 2025, where he won 9.9 per cent of first preferences. One Nation's candidate page refused automated requests, so it could not be checked.

prior_roles.role: Member of the Royal Australian Air Force

sources.title: Brunswick: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Adam Pulford is the Greens candidate for Brunswick at the 2026 Victorian election, the seat held by the late Greens MP Tim Read. A Merri-bek councillor since 2020, he served as mayor from 2023 to 2024. He was earlier a media adviser to federal Greens parliamentarians Richard Di Natale and Adam Bandt, and he ran unsuccessfully for the federal seat of Wills in 2019.

prior_roles.role: Media adviser to Richard Di Natale and Adam Bandt

priorities.text: representatives who actually work for people, not corporate profits
Cheaper rents and more affordable housing
Full funding for public schools, hospitals and health services
Replacing coal and gas with renewables and charging big polluters for climate damage

summary.text: Gabe Steger is Labor's candidate for Brunswick at the 2026 Victorian election. He advises Ged Kearney, the federal Labor member and assistant minister, and before that was a Commonwealth public servant in the prime minister's department and the Attorney-General's Department. Labor's page adds that he has headed a not-for-profit and rents in the area, and the ABC notes that he speaks Mandarin.

occupation.text: Adviser to federal Labor MP Ged Kearney

prior_roles.organisation: Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet

priorities.text: Half-price public transport fares to cut costs and emissions
Keeping Urgent Care Clinics, free kinder and free TAFE
Protecting the option of working from home

summary.text: India Rose is standing for the Animal Justice Party in Brunswick at the 2026 Victorian election. She runs Somewhere Soft, a business providing NDIS supports, which she started after more than six years in community services spanning youth work, homelessness programs and youth arts. Originally from Tasmania, she has lived in Victoria for about 15 years; an animal advocate since childhood, she joined Melbourne's vegan activist community after moving to the city.

occupation.text: Owner of an NDIS support service

prior_roles.role: Community services worker (youth work, homelessness services, youth arts, crisis response)

priorities.text: Stronger legal protection for animals
Care for the environment and nature
Listening to local residents and following up on their concerns

sources.title: Brunswick: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
India Rose for Brunswick, Animal Justice Party Victoria

summary.text: Jack Amanatidis is an independent candidate for Brunswick at the 2026 Victorian election. A civil engineer, he has worked for large construction firms as well as for councils and state agencies, according to the ABC. No campaign website or other published biography had been found as at early November 2026.

summary.text: Melissa Yuan is running as an independent in Brunswick at the 2026 Victorian election. She works in IT after an earlier career as a school teacher, has lived in Brunswick since 2002 and has two children at local schools. She helps run Brunswick Communities for Nature, a volunteer group that grows indigenous plants for green spaces, and her platform stresses evidence-based policy, education and open government.

previous_candidacies.note: Her campaign site carries her opening statement to a 2020 candidates forum about South Ward; no source found gives the result or confirms the label she stood under.

priorities.text: put people and evidence before party politics
Less bureaucracy for teachers and better teacher retention
More openness and accountability in government decisions
Clearer planning decisions and better-designed housing
Urban greening that supports biodiversity

summary.text: Naomi Farmer is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Brunswick at the 2026 Victorian election. A disability support worker raised in the Latrobe Valley, she has spent more than two decades as an activist in causes such as refugee rights, Palestine solidarity and marriage equality. She says that during the Hazelwood mine fire in her home town she wrote the first news story about it and organised the first protest.

priorities.text: challenge growing inequality, war, racism, and the climate catastrophe
Standing up to billionaires and the major parties for working-class people
Reversing cuts to public services

sources.title: Brunswick: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Naomi Farmer, Victorian Socialists
